# 批量初筛：v4.7.3（引擎 v4.7.2）

Rules version **2026-10-23c** (engine v4.7.2; skill text v4.7.3). This is the Codex port of the Claude skill of the same name; the numerical rules and scoring logic follow the supplied engine; source labels and local runtime/storage are adapted for this Workspace. A screen for deciding where to spend research time, so every measure is a fact: a number calculated from reported financials (the company's or its peers'), or a fact read from a primary document (10-K, proxy, 8-K, annual report, AGM results, SEC release). No judgment scores. Each company gets three separate lights, never combined: Business, Industry and Management (green ✓ / yellow half circle / red ✗), and one action label that answers "should research time go here now?", from the Business and Management lights, the red flags, where its multiples sit in their own history and whether they are getting cheaper. The user decides. The first table must stay short and intuitive; the detail lives in each company section. Version history, approvals and test results: `CHANGELOG.md`; it is not needed to run the screen.

## What the skill produces

1. For each company: B1–B4, I1–I3 and M1–M3, each set on a fixed 1–5 rule and shown as a light; the three factor lights (a range when a measure is missing); P/E, EV/EBIT and EV/EBITDA each as a percentile of the stock's own history and their median; a research line (share price); the direction (getting cheaper, steady, getting dearer) and today's multiples against their own median over 1, 3, 5 and 10 years; the forward P/E; the accounting red-flag check; the financial risk gate; the action label with its reason lines; and flags.
2. One HTML file: a map of where each company lands (Business light against where its multiples sit in their own history, each box titled with its action, and a hatched "Not judged yet" band for red flags, too-early names and open Business lights), then a short results table (Result label with its lines, one light each for Business, Industry and Management with a CEO-change tag under the Management light, multiples in their own history with the direction and the 1/3/5/10-year comparison, flags; no measure-level detail), a multiples strip chart, a table of what changed since the previous run (when there is one), the open points, the peer groups of the coverage universe (one box per tag with its companies listed, grouped by parent), and for each company a score build-up section in coloured panels: a Result card and a scorecard (one tile per measure with its 1–5 score and key number), the multiples table and a P/E history chart, the red-flag checks with sources, every measure led by its result with its inputs, bar charts of year-by-year series, rule and sources, the peer table behind Industry, and the information items and perimeter checks folded to one line each (see "The score build-up section" under Rules).
3. When the universe is new or changed: a CSV of every company in it with its tag and the reason, for the user to correct.
4. A numbered list of definition problems found in the run, for the user to decide.
5. **Screening records (v4.3)**: one permanent note per screened company in the vault folder `research/screens/records/` (`<Company> - 初筛记录.md`, relative to the Workspace root), created or updated on every run, and a "Look again" section on the HTML page listing the companies whose reopen condition the run met. See "Screening records" under Rules.

## Before you start: tools this skill needs

1. **FocusAlpha MCP is primary.** Discover relevant current tools and check issuer, periods and coverage before querying. For gaps or unavailable access, record the reason and use regulator, exchange or company IR originals. Follow the shared policy in `SKILL.md` and `focusalpha-normalization.md`. Fiscal.ai is disabled and never a prerequisite or fallback.
2. **Save complete outputs to files.** Preserve raw responses and originals under `$RUN/raw_sources/`, then normalize reproducibly. Do not reconstruct truncated bulk responses by hand. `source_ledger.json` records actual tools, periods, units and documents; `page_text.json.sources` and measure notes identify actual sources in the page. Read [valuation-reliability.md](valuation-reliability.md) for the required batch coverage and delivery checks; Gangtise numeric fallback and research evidence have separate roles under `gangtise-screening.md`.
3. **Workspace Python** with `pypdf` and `beautifulsoup4` (`"$PY" -m pip install pypdf beautifulsoup4`); `pdftotext` where PDF extraction is needed. Node + Playwright for screenshots; use an existing available runtime before installing.
4. **Privacy:** never put the user's email or personal data in headers, URLs or User-Agent strings.

## Source of truth

- The rules in this SKILL.md and in `RULES` (top of `screener.py`) are the imported upstream rules; `CHANGELOG.md` records approvals and cases from the original environment. This installation imports those rules for future batch runs only.
- Measures decided against; do not add them back without the user's approval: judgment or reviewer scores; B5; M4; a peer cap on B4; I4 and segment weighting; direction markers on the old quadrant; peer ROIC or peer valuation as a Business measure; consensus valuation and a forward P/E history (no data; left for later research stages); vesting horizon; FCF margin and CFO ÷ net income (B2 covers them); positive-EBIT years (B1 covers them); stock comp ÷ revenue (stock comp ÷ operating income is used).
- Existing runs keep their recorded rules version. Installing an update does not rescreen companies or rewrite records. On a requested refresh, treat a version change as a rules change (Step 6, point 6).
- The Claude Doc **"Stock Screener Scoring Definitions"** (id `d6ed49f9-883e-426a-9f1c-c512886c0a64`) still describes v1 (judgment measures, Fiscal.ai peer lists, a five-measure Industry factor). Do not follow it where it differs. Treat it as historical material; do not edit unrelated external documents as part of screening.

## Settle these before starting

Ask in the chat only when the request leaves one of these open; otherwise use the default and say so.
1. **The list.** A file or a list of tickers. Use only the columns the user asks for; ask before applying a filter-looking column. Unattended default: all rows.
2. **Non-SEC companies.** Default: score them, with the non-SEC red-flag check; M1/M2 from the annual report, remuneration report and AGM results.
3. **Excluded sectors** (banks, insurers, asset managers, REITs, lessors, SPACs, funds, trusts). Default: skip and list them.
4. **Fact-collection scope.** Up to about 30 names: every company. Larger lists: run Step 3 first, then collect facts only for names with Business ≥ 3.0 (or a range reaching 3.0) plus short-history names. Never skip the red-flag check for a green or yellow Business light.

## Workflow

Keep a step list and tick it off. Initialize from the Workspace root. Raw and working files stay in `sources/screens/<run-id>/`; HTML and screenshots go in `outputs/screens/<run-id>/`.

### Step 0. Engine files

```bash
WORKSPACE_ROOT="$(pwd)"
SKILL_DIR="$WORKSPACE_ROOT/.github/skills/stock-initial-screen"
PY="$WORKSPACE_ROOT/.venv/bin/python"
RUN_ID="<short-name>-<YYYY-MM-DD>"
RUN="$WORKSPACE_ROOT/sources/screens/$RUN_ID"
U="$RUN/universe"
OUT="$WORKSPACE_ROOT/outputs/screens/$RUN_ID"
NOTES="$WORKSPACE_ROOT/research/screens/records"
mkdir -p "$RUN/raw" "$RUN/raw_sources" "$RUN/facts" "$RUN/scratch" "$U/raw" "$OUT/shots"
cp "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/screener.py" "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/make_html.py" "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/redesign.py" "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/vault_records.py" "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/shot.js" "$RUN/"
cp "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/valuation_pipeline.py" "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/checked_build.py" "$RUN/"
cp "$SKILL_DIR/references/fact_brief_template.md" "$SKILL_DIR/references/config_example.json" "$RUN/"
```

Verify copied files against `SKILL_DIR/references/engine-checksums.json` (SHA-256). Checksums describe this local port; numerical scoring rules match the imported engine. On an unexpected mismatch, identify the changed file before running; do not rebuild engine code from memory. Fiscal.ai connector/templates remain in the skill for provenance and old-run compatibility only and are not copied or executed.

### Step 1. Resolve company identities and source keys

Use FocusAlpha `search_companies` to confirm company, ticker, market and primary listing. Build `$RUN/config.json` from `config_example.json`: `key`, `name`, `group`; `key` is the stable join key shared by run data and universe data, not a requirement to use any provider's identifier. Existing universe keys may keep their historical spelling. Reconcile listing changes as one issuer with a documented continuous history.

### Step 1b. Read the screening records (vault)

The Workspace holds one record per screened company in `research/screens/records/`. Read them before pulling data, using `$NOTES` initialized in Step 0. The Obsidian vault root is the Workspace parent.
1. `"$PY" "$RUN/vault_records.py" read "$RUN" "$NOTES"` → `$RUN/prior_records.json` (frontmatter of the records for the run's tickers). Say in the first progress message how many of the run's companies have a record and their recorded labels.
2. Inspect `research/companies/<market>/<ticker-slug>/` for existing research and decision notes. Link relevant notes with Workspace-relative paths from the durable summary.
3. If the vault folder is not reachable, say so, run without records, and save the record files beside the HTML for the user to add; never write records from memory.

### Step 2. Pull the data

Read `focusalpha-normalization.md` and `valuation-reliability.md` for the exact contracts and required coverage checks. Obtain statements, daily prices, share data and filings from relevant FocusAlpha tools, saving complete paginated originals. Normalize by fiscal year, issuer, listing, currency and share basis; do not silently skip IFRS, non-USD or dimensioned share classes. Log the FocusAlpha gap, inspect useful Gangtise data tools, and verify financial facts against original disclosures. Missing values remain null with reasons. Use the staged build/promote commands in `valuation-reliability.md`; new batches keep `valuation_pipeline_required=true`.

1. `raw/main1.json`, `main2.json`, …: annual financials in millions of reporting currency; collect enough opening balance sheets for the latest 10 reported years. Keep the supplied column names. Repair acquired-intangible amortization, impairment and continuing CFO from filings; do not mistake D&A or operating-profit subtotals for amortization.
2. `raw/pe.json`: daily trailing GAAP P/E plus current price, market cap and optional forward P/E. `raw/ev.json`: daily EV/EBIT, EV/EBITDA, enterprise value and price. If derived, label as analysis calculations and retain input sources and publication dates. Never use later financials to reconstruct earlier ratios.
3. History may be shorter than 10 years. Record actual coverage; absent historical market caps or debt prevent a reliable EV history. Retain N/A where needed rather than fabricate it or enable Fiscal.ai. A current ratio is not a daily history.
4. Listing change: join reconciled histories under the scoring key, using each listing only on its applicable dates; document split, spin-off, ADR and currency treatment.

### Step 2b. Coverage universe and peers (Industry)

Peers come from a coverage universe: one file listing the companies the user follows in a sector, each with one sub-industry tag and the reason. The Industry group is every company with the same tag, the run company included (v4.7), so every company in a tag gets the same Industry light.
1. Use `$U` initialized in Step 0, with `raw/`. Copy the matching file from `SKILL_DIR/references/` to `$U/universe.json`: `universe_aero_industrials.json` (aerospace and industrial components, 73 companies; checksum `83963e64e52c2f00`), `universe_beverages.json` (beverages, bottlers, coffee and beverage shops, nutrition, packaged food with beverages, 68 companies; `e65f2009edf44674`) or `universe_services_distribution_transport.json` (services, distribution, freight transport and building products, 67 companies, 9 tags, 4 parent groups; `e18e7c2c5978555b`). A checksum changes whenever the user corrects tags. Set `"universe_dir"` in `config.json`.
2. Every run company must be in the universe; for a missing one propose a tag from the FocusAlpha company profile and filed segment mix and tell the user. A new sector gets a new universe (40–60 names, PM-style sub-industry tags, a `def` sentence per tag, parent groups, an `excluded` list).
3. Known separations: `window_from`/`window_why` for peers whose earlier years are a different business. A run company used as a peer keeps its `perimeter_start` from the run config.
4. Normalize peer financials from FocusAlpha first into `$U/raw/peers.json`; copy the run's `raw/main*.json` into `$U/raw/`. Apply consistent definitions to the whole group and log any original-disclosure fallback. Do not apply screened-company-specific fact repairs to other peers except the established amortization and settlement adjustments. Fixed-schedule settlement liabilities (v4.7): fixed-schedule settlement liabilities go into `$U/raw_extra/debt_like.json` (`{"companies": {<key>: {"label", "years": {FY: {"noncurrent", "current"}}, "source"}}}`), so every company in a group is measured on the same debt definition. For the services universe copy `SKILL_DIR/references/debt_like_services_distribution_transport.json` there (McKesson, Cardinal Health and Cencora opioid settlements). For a new universe, screen each member's as-reported balance sheet and litigation notes through FocusAlpha or original disclosures for litigation or settlement lines; self-insurance reserves and landfill or environmental obligations are not settlements.
4b. Amortization of acquired intangibles for US-listed peers: keep it separate from D&A; take it from FocusAlpha `get_cash_flow_statements` (annual) and write `$U/raw_extra/am_focusalpha.json` as `{"companies": {<key>: {"rows": [{"report_period", "net_income", "amortization"}]}}}`; the engine matches each row to the normalized fiscal year whose net income agrees within 2%, else by the period-end year. Non-US peers retain the normalized source basis; flag any missing amortization. Avoid double-counting amortization already present in normalized rows. Peers come only from universe tags, not an unreviewed provider peer list.
5. A tag with fewer than 6 companies with an I1 value is marked "thin group" (v4.7): one company's data moves its median, so read the group table.
6. When the universe is new or changed, write it as a CSV (ticker, key, company, tag, parent, reason, GICS, window) for the user to correct.

### Step 3. Data measures, perimeter flags and data checks

`"$PY" "$RUN/screener.py" "$RUN" score` prints the B1–B4 inputs and scores, stock comp ÷ operating income, M3, the perimeter flags (revenue moves above 25%, goodwill + intangibles moves above 25% of invested capital, share jumps above 50%) and the data checks (amortization missing, discontinued operations in the cash flow, stock comp missing). Also check tax rates outside 0–50%, fewer than 10 years and jumps that look like data errors.

### Step 4. Fact collectors (one per company)

1. Write `$RUN/fact_brief.md` from `fact_brief_template.md` with `str.replace` (not `.format`): `{AS_OF}`, `{RUN_DIR}`, `{SINCE_402}` = as-of minus 3 years, `{SINCE_AAER}` = as-of minus 5 years, `{PRIOR_FILES_NOTE}` = empty or a pointer to an earlier run's fact files. The adapted brief already specifies FocusAlpha first, original-disclosure fallback and optional Gangtise context; do not reinsert upstream Fiscal.ai or Claude-only tool recipes.
2. One collector per company, each writing only `facts/<TICKER>.json` and its own `scratch/<TICKER>/` folder. If this Codex build can start sub-agents, start one per company. Otherwise run them from the shell in parallel with Codex's non-interactive mode (`codex exec`), at most about 8 at a time, or one after another in this session. Prompt:

   > You are a fact collector for the company initial screener (v4). Read the brief at `<RUN>/fact_brief.md` and follow it exactly. Your company: `<TICKER>` — `<name>` (stable engine key `<KEY>`, FocusAlpha identity and CIK if known). `<SEC registrant or not>`. Latest fiscal year in the data: FY`<L>`, reporting currency `<cur>`. Window years: FY`<L−9>`–FY`<L>`. Years flagged by the data (explain each): `<flags>`. Data notes: `<data checks>`. Known context: `<deals, IPO, listing changes, earlier red flags>`. Write `<RUN>/facts/<TICKER>.json` and reply with the 5–8 line summary the brief asks for.

3. Check that each JSON parses; read every red flag, flagged year and data repair. A collector takes about 7–15 minutes.

### Step 5. Perimeter and windows (config.json)

Set per company, from the facts: `perimeter_start` (first full fiscal year with both balance sheets after a deal that moved revenue more than 25%, a separation or disposal not restated, or a share jump above 50%; **a deal flagged only by the goodwill test gets no `perimeter_start`**: the engine keeps the window and takes the lower of the full-window and post-deal B1/B4 by itself, v4.4), `deal_flags_ok` (a deal flag inside the window that does not break it, with the reason; a year listed here is also left out of the post-deal test and, since v4.7.1, does not make the deal count as big; list the first full year after a big deal that starts the window here, as for RBC's Dodge FY2023 or Kraft Heinz FY2016), `post_deal_from` (override of the first post-deal year), `held_for_sale` (`{years, why}`: balance sheets that carry a sold unit only as held for sale count when the income statement is restated; flagged), `b3_mix` (one line when B3 mixes sold businesses or two accounting standards; flag only), `growth_start`/`growth_start_why` (after a spin-off or separation), `downturn`, `dil_base`, `pe_from`/`pe_from_why` (the deal date itself; the engine starts every multiple's window 12 months later; a listing needs none), `pe_now_override` (when the daily P/E has stopped updating: price ÷ (latest full-year EPS − prior-year interim EPS + current-year interim EPS), arithmetic in `why`), `perimeter_note`, `red_flag_overrides` (only when a red flag is plainly wrong on its own quoted source), `measure_gaps` (plain reason a measure cannot be filled). **B3 substitute after a separation:** when B3 is not scored because a separation left fewer than 6 clean years, collect the predecessor segment operating profit of today's businesses from the former parent's filings into `facts/<T>_b3sub.json`; accept it only with one profit definition across the years and no exclusion of recurring costs (Crane accepted; Melrose's adjusted profit rejected).

### Step 6. Assemble and check

`"$PY" "$RUN/checked_build.py" "$RUN"` runs the unchanged numerical engine with source-completeness eligibility checks and writes `page_data.json` and `universe_page.json`. Then run `"$PY" "$RUN/valuation_pipeline.py" annotate "$RUN"` to reconcile each multiple's history state with the engine and export `valuation_coverage.csv`. For a valuation-only partial repair use `valuation_pipeline.py refresh` instead, preserving non-target companies and every quality score. Then:
1. Spot-check three companies by hand (one green on Business, one with a red flag, one short history), one peer ROIC and one group median.
2. Confirm the quote behind every red flag says what the rule needs. Every AAER, removing or not: check `conduct_end` (the end of the misconduct the order describes) against the order or press release; the 5-year horizon counts from it (Rollins, 23 Oct 2026: SEC press release 2022-64 says Q1 2016 and Q2 2017 and "multiple additional quarters from 2016 through 2018"; no last quarter stated, so 2018-12-31). Every `debt_like` entry in a fact file (litigation settlements paid on a fixed schedule): check the balance against the balance sheet or the litigation note, both parts (v4.7: the non-current line and the current part from the litigation note; McKesson: "Long-term litigation liabilities" $5,091m and current $601m at Mar 2026, the filed balance sheet and litigation note). Several settlements go in as named items (since v4.7.1).
3. Every "Multiples disagree" line on a name that is not "Not now": find the cause in the filings and write a note (Crane: discontinued operations in trailing net income through Q1 2026, and the January 2026 PSI acquisition raised interest expense from $11.3m to $35.9m; FocusAlpha income statements, trailing 12 months). For a name within 5% of its research line, compare the normalized same-day net debt (enterprise value − market value) with the latest filed net debt (FocusAlpha balance sheets) and say whether the label would change (Crane on 20 Oct 2026: $750.5m against $748.0m filed, so the line stood). Take both from the same day.
4. Write `page_text.json`: `sources` must identify exact tools, periods, coverage and source-ledger paths, with calculated ratios labelled as calculations; use company `measure_notes` / fact evidence to identify sources where they differ. Then add `lead` (four to six sentences, one per action label: which names and the one fact that put them there; then the note that the multiples are not a valuation), `problems` (definition problems with proposed fixes), `notes` per company.
5. If config or source events changed, rebuild/promote the affected valuation inputs, then re-run checked build and annotate (or scoped refresh). Do not leave stale coverage notes, CSV or snapshots from an earlier build.
6. **Compare with the screening records (v4.3).** `"$PY" "$RUN/vault_records.py" snapshot "$RUN"`, then `"$PY" "$RUN/vault_records.py" compare "$RUN"` → `$RUN/reopen.json`. For every company with a record it lists what changed (label, lights, measure scores, median percentile, direction, flags, CEO) and gives each change a cause: business (a new fiscal year in the data, a CEO change), price, rules, data, filing or peers; only a business cause can mean the case has changed. It applies the record's reopen test and sets **Look again** with the reasons, otherwise **No action**. Re-look signals are compared by what they are about (a CEO change by month, a deal by name; v4.7.1), so a reworded signal in an older record is not counted as new. When the rules version changed since a record, rebuild the newest run archive under the new engine (unzip it to `$RUN/baseline/`, point its `universe_dir` at the archived universe, set its `rules_version` to the engine's `RULES_VERSION` or delete the key, since v4.7.2 `build` stops on another rules version; then `build` and `snapshot` it) and pass `--baseline "$RUN/baseline/snapshot.json"`, so rules effects are labelled `rules`. Check every `data` and `filing` cause before delivery. Fill `page_text.json` `moves` from `reopen.json`; `make_html.py` shows the Look again section by itself when `reopen.json` exists.

### Step 7. HTML and visual check

**Chinese delivery requirement.** Read [chinese-report-style.md](chinese-report-style.md). Set `report_language="zh-CN"` in new batch configurations. Write narrative inputs in professional, connected Chinese, then localize every remaining static label, tooltip and dynamic button after generation. The upstream English template is an intermediate artifact. Preserve all financial inputs, scores, meanings, source links and interactive anchors; review Chinese prose and test the final localized HTML before Step 8. User requests limited to translating an existing HTML do not authorize a new financial run or record update.

```bash
"$PY" "$RUN/make_html.py" "$RUN"
NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g) node "$RUN/shot.js" "$RUN/<output>.html" "$OUT/shots" <T1>,<T2>
```
Look at the screenshots: the map (no ticker label crossing a divider or another label; the no-multiple column complete; every red-flag, too-early and open-light name in the hatched "Not judged yet" band with its reason line readable and no label running past the right edge; every note box in its colour with ▸ and its count, one note opened and "Show all notes" read cleanly, no ticker moved) and the results table in light and dark mode (one light per factor, colour and symbol only, grey ? where a missing measure decides the colour, nothing crowded), one company's Industry section with its peer table, the peer-group section, the multiples strip (shapes must not hide each other's labels), one company's multiples table and trend lines, the peer-group boxes, one company with a red flag, one with a short perimeter, and the mobile view. In the score build-up section: one company's scorecard (score chips coloured by light, Pass or Fail on the two gates, no tile text cut off), its bar charts (labels readable over the dashed median), a red-flag company (only the flagged check red and open; a check that is not a red flag under the rule, such as no ICFR report yet for a newly public company, grey), a company whose window a deal cut (Perimeter open with its tag), every panel closed (each keeps its header line; a scorecard tile reopens its panel), an Industry measure marked near the cut-off, and the phone view (tiles two across, rows one column, nothing off the right edge). `make_html.py` stops if `redesign.py` rewrote fewer company sections than the run has. Fix and rebuild.

### Step 8. Deliver

Run `"$PY" "$RUN/valuation_pipeline.py" check "$RUN" --html "$RUN/<output>.html"` and resolve every error before delivery. Warnings are documented unresolved gaps, not requests for permission. Verify the copied HTML too; copy `valuation_audit.json`, `valuation_coverage.csv`, `source_ledger.json` and `data_quality_gaps.json` beside it. Every unplaced company must distinguish a nonpositive denominator, actual short history and a source gap; current/approximate multiples are shown separately from historical percentile eligibility. Refresh the summary, records and manifest from the final data, preserving old archives and user-owned fields.

Copy the verified HTML to `$OUT/` and open it; save a new or changed universe CSV there too. Keep source originals and the run archive under `$RUN/`; put a durable conclusion with relative links in `research/screens/`. In the reply: premise check, conclusion (Research now and Quick look names first), evidence, the definition problems to decide (numbered, each with the proposed fix), uncertainty. Never combine the three factors into one score. Never describe a multiple's percentile as attractiveness or a buy signal ("50th percentile does not mean valuation is becoming more attractive, nor does 33rd mean it fits a buy decision"); valuation is checked later against the 15% hurdle.

**Screening records (v4.3, vault rule 20).** After the HTML: `"$PY" "$RUN/vault_records.py" write "$RUN" "$NOTES" --run-file "outputs/screens/$RUN_ID/<output HTML name>" --industry <the vault 行业 name, e.g. 航空航天> --vault "$WORKSPACE_ROOT"`. It creates a note for a new company and, for an existing one, rewrites only its own frontmatter fields and the "Latest" block and inserts one history row at the top. It never writes `our_decision`, `our_reason`, `our_reopen_if`, `our_check_date` or the "Your notes" section, and it skips a company whose record already holds this run. Do not run it while the user has the note open for editing. In the reply put the Look again companies first under the conclusion, with the reason; never describe a Look again company as a buy.

**Run archive.** Also save `<output stem>_screener_run_<as_of>.zip` under `$RUN/` and link it from the summary (page_data.json, run_meta.json, universe_page.json, config.json, page_text.json, source_ledger.json, valuation inputs/audit/coverage, delivery_check.json, facts/, facts_model/, raw/, raw_sources/ and the universe folder with its peer data); later reruns and the initial dive read it. A same-cutoff repair gets a new revision archive; do not overwrite the prior archive.

## Rules (version 2026-10-23c; all thresholds are in `RULES` at the top of screener.py)

**Lights.** Every measure is set on 1–5 by its rule, and the arithmetic is shown; the page shows a light: 4–5 green ✓, 3 yellow half circle (an inline SVG; the "!" read as an error and "◐" rendered too small), 1–2 red ✗, not scored grey –. A factor light comes from the average of its measures: 3.5 or more green, 3.0 to 3.5 yellow, below 3.0 red. A missing measure is first filled with a filed fact where one exists (see the B3 substitute). If it stays missing, it makes a range (missing = 1 to missing = 5). If both ends give the same colour, that colour is shown; if the colour depends on the missing measure, the light is a grey ? whose hover text names the measure and the reason ("not disclosed" differs from "too new"). Never fill a gap with an assumed value such as 3 (the user rejected it), and never show two symbols side by side (the user found them confusing). Business, Industry and Management are never combined. The 1–5 score itself is shown in one place only: the scorecard chips in each company section (the user asked on 2026-10-21); the results table and the map stay symbol-only.

**Data and window.** Fiscal years; latest 10 reported years, or the current perimeter if shorter. Average capital = (opening + closing) ÷ 2, so each year needs the prior year's balance sheet. Amounts in reporting currency. Amortization, impairments and continuing operating cash flow are repaired from filings where the data source lacks them.

**Shared formulas.**
- NOPAT = (operating income + amortization of acquired intangibles + goodwill and intangible impairments) × (1 − 25%).
- Invested capital including goodwill = debt + lease liabilities + debt-like liabilities + total equity − cash. Debt-like liabilities (v4.4) = litigation or regulatory settlements paid on a fixed schedule over several years, from the fact file (`data.debt_like`; one item, a flat year list, or since v4.7.1 several named items, which are added together); they also count in net debt for the financial risk gate. Both parts count (v4.7): the non-current line and the current part, which usually sits inside accrued liabilities and comes from the litigation note; when the current part is not disclosed the page flags "Settlement debt: current part not disclosed … debt is understated". The same definition applies to every company in an Industry group (`$U/raw_extra/debt_like.json`), so a run company and its peers are measured alike.
- Capital excluding goodwill = that − goodwill (acquired intangibles stay in).
- FCF = CFO from continuing operations + capex (negative as filed) − stock comp.

**Business** (its own factor light, the average of B1–B4; a missing measure gives a range from "missing = 1" to "missing = 5"; never average only the available measures)
- **B1 return on capital excluding goodwill (core).** NOPAT ÷ average capital excluding goodwill, each year of the window. Median: ≥25% → 5, ≥15% → 4, ≥10% → 3, ≥6% → 2, else 1. 25th-percentile year (k-th lowest, k = ceil(n × 0.25): 3rd lowest of 10, lowest of 3–4): ≥15% → 5, ≥10% → 4, ≥6% → 3, else 2. B1 = lower; median below 6% → 1. A year with capital excluding goodwill ≤ 0 uses ROIC including goodwill. After a separation, B1 drops one level if the predecessor segment's lowest 3-year average margin is below 50% of its median. After a deal flagged only by the goodwill test (see Perimeter), B1 = the lower of this score and the median-threshold score of the average of the years after the deal.
- **B2 cash conversion.** (FCF + net interest × (1 − t)) ÷ ((operating income + impairments) × (1 − t)) over the B1 window. t = total tax ÷ total pre-tax income; 25% if pre-tax ≤ 0 or t outside 0–50%. ≥100% → 5, ≥90% → 4, ≥75% → 3, ≥50% → 2, else 1; cumulative FCF ≤ 0 or NOPAT ≤ 0 → 1.
- **B3 growth in NOPAT per share** (or the filed substitute after a separation, Step 5). NOPAT ÷ diluted shares; from the median of the first 3 years to the median of the last 3 years of the 10-year window (medians so one bad year, such as MTU's 2023 GTF charge, does not decide it), so the midpoints are n − 3 years apart (7 for 10 years). Acquisitions stay in; a spin-off or separation (`growth_start`) or a one-year diluted-share jump above 50% starts the window later; needs 6 years; an end point ≤ 0 → not scored. ≥12% → 5, ≥8% → 4, ≥5% → 3, ≥2% → 2, else 1 (12% growth + about 3% cash yield ≈ the 15% hurdle at an unchanged P/E). Revenue growth on the same method is shown as information.
- **B4 return on all capital, including goodwill.** Median of NOPAT ÷ average invested capital including goodwill over the B1 window: ≥15% → 5, ≥12% → 4, ≥9% → 3, ≥6% → 2, else 1. It charges for the price paid for acquisitions, which B3 counts as growth. After a deal flagged only by the goodwill test, B4 = the lower of the full-window score and the score of the average of the years after the deal (WM, 23 Oct 2026: full window 12.5% → 4, FY2025 after Stericycle 11.0% → 3, B4 = 3).

**Management** (its own factor light, the average of M1–M3; not combined with the others)
- **M1 CEO ownership.** Shares owned excluding options and unvested awards × today's price ÷ base salary: ≥30× or founder/family ≥5% with an active role → 5, ≥15× → 4, ≥6× → 3, ≥2× → 2, else 1. +1 if officers and directors were net open-market buyers over 24 months; −1 if the CEO sold more than 30% of held shares, but the penalty cannot take M1 below 2 (`m1_sale_floor`, v4.7, user 2026-10-23): a holding that already scores 1 or 2 shows the result of the selling, so the same sales are not counted twice. The sale record stays in the row. No ownership-guideline test.
- **M2 cost of stock pay and the pay vote.** Lower of (a) stock comp ÷ operating income, sums over the latest 5 fiscal years: <3% → 5, 3–6% → 4, 6–10% → 3, 10–15% → 2, >15% → 1 (operating income ≤ 0 → 1), and (b) the latest say-on-pay (US) or remuneration-report vote (UK, Germany), For ÷ (For + Against): ≥90% → 5, 80–90% → 4, 70–80% → 3, 50–70% → 2, <50% → 1. One alone if the other is missing.
- **CEO changes (display only; the user asked on 2026-10-21 for a recent management change to show more obviously under Management, traced back 5 years).** From the collector's `ceo_since` and `ceo_changes_5y` (every CEO change in the last 5 years, with the announcement as source). A CEO in office for less than 5 years (`ceo_trace_years`) gets a tag directly under the Management light in the results table and beside it in the company summary bar: amber "New CEO · <month year>" under 24 months (`new_ceo_months`), grey "CEO since <month year>" from 2 to 5 years, plus "· N changes in 5 yrs" when there were two or more. The Management block of the company section opens with one line: who changed and when, then how many of the years behind each measure fall under the current CEO (M1 is the current CEO's own holding; M2 stock pay x of 5 fiscal years; the pay vote covers the last fiscal year ended before the meeting; M3 write-downs x of n years and share count x of n years), and whether most of those years are under this CEO or earlier ones. A fiscal year counts when the CEO held the job for at least 6 of its 12 months. The tag itself changes no measure, light or label; M3 uses the same year count to choose its window (v4.7). The "Re-look signal" / "Note: new CEO" line under the Result stays at 24 months.
- **M3 capital allocation record.** Window (v4.7, user 2026-10-23): the current CEO's fiscal years when the B1 window holds at least 5 of them (`m3_ceo_min_years`; a year counts when the CEO held the job for 6 of its 12 months, as for the CEO tag), otherwise the full B1 window, with "mostly the previous CEO's record" when fewer than half its years are under the current CEO. Two columns, average rounded down, both needed: (goodwill and intangible impairments + losses on businesses sold or held for sale, less any filed release of past currency-translation losses) over the window ÷ average goodwill + intangibles over the window (0 → 5, <5% → 4, <15% → 3, <30% → 2, else 1); diluted share change from the year before the window (FY(L−10) for the full window, the first perimeter year, or `dil_base`) to FY(L) (≤−15% → 5, ≤−5% → 4, ≤+5% → 3, ≤+20% → 2, else 1). Losses on businesses come from the fact file (`data.business_disposal_losses`); gains are shown, never netted; a fact file without the field (collected before v4.7) counts impairments only and the row says so. The losses are not added back to NOPAT (open decision D21).

**Industry** (its own factor light, the average of I1–I3; peers from the coverage universe, Step 2b)
- Group (v4.7, user 2026-10-23): every company in the tag with data, the run company included, so every company in a tag gets the same Industry light. A tag keeps its own group when at least 4 of its companies have an I1 value (`peer_tag_min`); otherwise the whole tag widens to the parent group (all tags under it, the run company included). I1 and I2 need 4 companies with a value (`group_min`); an I3 year needs 4 companies (`i3_min_cos`). The page puts the company count under the Industry light in the results table and marks a group with fewer than 6 companies with an I1 value "thin group" (`thin_group`); the group table marks the company itself. The line "Returns X% vs peers Y%" under the Result still compares the company with the others only (`peer_min` = 3 other companies over the company's own years).
- Group window: latest 10 fiscal years of normalized source data, no company-specific repairs except the established amortization and settlement adjustments (above). It starts later after a separation (revenue down more than 25% and goodwill + intangibles down more than 25% of invested capital in one year), a diluted-share jump above 50%, `window_from` in the universe, or the run's `perimeter_start` for a run company. Acquisitions stay in, because ROIC including goodwill charges the price paid. A profit subtotal that the line search mistakes for amortization or impairment ("operating profit before amortisation") is set to 0.
- **I1 industry return on all capital.** Each company in the group: median of NOPAT ÷ average invested capital including goodwill and settlement liabilities (B4 formula), needs 5 years; capital ≤ 0 in 3 or more years counts as top of the range. Group value = median across the group. ≥15% → 5, ≥12% → 4, ≥9% → 3, ≥6% → 2, else 1.
- **I2 industry revenue growth.** Each company in the group: median revenue of its first 3 years to the median of its last 3 years, as a yearly rate (B3 method), needs 6 years; includes acquisitions. Group value = median across the group. ≥10% → 5, ≥7% → 4, ≥4% → 3, ≥2% → 2, else 1.
- **I3 depth of the worst industry year.** For each of the last 10 fiscal years, the median revenue change across the group (a year needs 4 companies); the worst year: better than −5% → 5, better than −10% → 4, better than −20% → 3, better than −30% → 2, else 1. The second-worst year is shown beside it. FY2020 stays in as the depth of a real downturn (the user's decision); do not drop a year because it was unusual.
- **Near the cut-off (v4.7.1, user 2026-10-23; display only).** An I1, I2 or I3 group value within 1 percentage point of a score cut-off (`near_cut`) gets "(near the cut-off)" in its headline and a note with the distance ("7.3% is 0.3 points above the 7% line, so one company more or less in the group can move this score"). When one score step on that measure would change the Industry light, the flags say "Industry light near a cut-off: I2 (…) — one step on that measure would change the light". No score moves. Reason: in a group of 8–10 companies one company more or less moves a median across a line (the waste tag's growth median sits at 7.3% against the 7% line).

**Accounting red flags (shown in red in the results table and listed last; such a company should not get research time until the issue is resolved).** SEC registrants: an 8-K Item 4.02 non-reliance filed in the last 3 years; a material weakness at the latest fiscal year-end (management's ineffective conclusion or the auditor's adverse ICFR opinion); an SEC Accounting and Auditing Enforcement Release naming the company, a subsidiary or an officer, for misconduct that ended in the last 5 years. The AAER horizon counts from the end of the misconduct the release describes (`conduct_end` in the fact file; `RULES['redflag_aaer_basis'] = 'conduct'`), not from the release date (user, 2026-10-23: Rollins' AAER No. 4294 of 18 Apr 2022 covers reserve cuts in 2016–2018, outside the horizon). Without `conduct_end` (fact files collected before v4.3.2) the release date is used. **An AAER whose misconduct ended earlier is not a red flag but stays highlighted** (user, 2026-10-23: "we still need to flag this issue using highlight, just not a reason to put it in the Not judged section"): the flag "Past SEC enforcement: <number> (<release date>), misconduct <years>; outside the 5-year horizon, not a red flag", a "Note: past SEC enforcement, …" line under the Result, an amber highlight behind the ticker on the map and in the flags column of the results table, an amber "!" row with its "How checked" note open in the red-flag panel, and "Past AAER" on the red-flag tile. The company is placed by its lights like any other. The 8-K Item 4.02 test still counts 3 years from the filing date (user, 2026-10-23: "for now keep the restatement from the filing date"). Non-SEC filers: a restatement the company itself calls an error correction in the last 3 years, a modified audit opinion on the latest accounts, or an accounting-regulator finding in the last 5 years (a re-presentation the company does not call an error is listed in the red-flag panel as information, since v4.7.1). Shown for information only: auditor changes and CFO departures in the last 5 years, share classes with different votes.

**Financial risk gate (a flag in the results table).** Latest fiscal year: net debt (debt + leases − cash) ÷ EBITDA (operating income + D&A) above 5×, or EBITDA ≤ 0 with net debt, or operating income ÷ gross interest expense below 2×.

**Perimeter.** A year counts only if its income statement and both balance sheets are on the current business (a balance sheet that carries a sold unit only as held for sale counts when the income statement is restated, flagged). Automatic flags: revenue change above 25% in a year; goodwill + intangibles change above 25% of prior-year invested capital; diluted shares up more than 50%. The fact collector names each flag's cause. A deal that moves revenue more than 25%, a separation or a share jump starts the window after it. **A deal flagged only by the goodwill test keeps the window (v4.4)**: B1 and B4 take the lower of the full window and the years after the deal, and the flag reads "Deal in FY<y> (goodwill test only): window kept; B1/B4 also on <years>, lower score used". Reason (user, 23 Oct 2026): the cut existed so that years before a deal, with less capital, do not flatter returns; only B1 and B4 divide by capital, so the deal is charged there and the history is kept for B2, B3 and Management. The rule never raises a score. A flag with no deal is cleared. Fewer than 3 clean years: the flag "short history" and the scores are shown for information. A deal above 25% of revenue after the latest year-end keeps the window and adds the flag "business changing".

**Multiples in their own history (replaces the P/E-only position).**
- Three daily multiples from normalized source inputs (FocusAlpha first; calculations identified with their sources): trailing P/E (price ÷ diluted GAAP EPS of the last four quarters), EV/EBIT and EV/EBITDA (enterprise value ÷ trailing operating profit and EBITDA). Each is placed in the stock's own history: percentile = share of positive days with a value ≤ today's. Window: 10 years; after `pe_from` (a merger, separation or data break) it starts 12 months later; a listing starts it at the first trading day. A multiple needs 250 positive days (about one year) and a positive value on 60% of days; otherwise "n/a" with the reason.
- The reading is the median of the available percentiles (two → their average, rounded half up), so one distorted multiple cannot set it. Percentiles 30 or more points apart → the Result adds "Multiples disagree: <highest>, <lowest>; check why" (Step 6.3 says how).
- Research line = the middle of the three share prices at which each multiple would sit at its own median: P/E price × median ÷ today; EV multiples: (enterprise value × median ÷ today − net debt) ÷ shares, with net debt = enterprise value − market value on the same day (the market value is re-priced to the enterprise-value date with the daily price series) and held at today's level. At that price the median percentile reaches the 50th, so it matches the Research now rule.
- **Direction (the signal the user cares most about).** For each multiple, today ÷ its own median over the last 1, 3, 5 and 10 years − 1 (clean window only; a horizon cut short by a deal or listing shows its real length, and horizons cut to the same window collapse into one cell); the reading is the median across the three multiples. "Getting cheaper" = 10% or more below the 1-year median (`cheaper_move`) AND below the multiple exactly one year ago (median across the three; up to a month earlier when the data has a gap). "Getting dearer" = the mirror. Otherwise "Steady"; no direction with under 0.9 clean years. Both tests are needed because a fall back from a spike is not a de-rating: RBC's P/E went 45.5× (Oct 2025) → 70.3× (Jun 2026) → 49.8×, 14% below its 1-year median but 4% above a year ago, so it is Steady. The results table shows the direction as a coloured chip (green "↓ Getting cheaper", grey "→ Steady", red "↑ Getting dearer"; the user asked for colour so the direction reads at a glance) and "vs own level: 1 yr · 3 yr · 5 yr · 10 yr"; the hover text gives each multiple's medians, the year-ago values and the single-day price/EPS split.
- Trend lines (company section): EV/EBITDA change from the close 3, 5 and 10 years ago to today (↓ or ↑ beyond ±10%, → otherwise), split into enterprise value and EBITDA: 1 + multiple change = (1 + EV change) ÷ (1 + EBITDA change). Hover text: the P/E split (price and EPS) and the last 12 months. A horizon that starts before the clean window (a deal plus 12 months, or a listing) is replaced by one "since <month year> (n yr)" line when that is at least 1 year; otherwise "n/a, business changed <month year>". EV/EBITDA is the trend metric because it stays positive through one-off losses (MTU's 2023 GTF charge made trailing P/E negative) and is not moved by interest, tax or acquisition amortization. Do not go back to a 12-month trend: the user found it too short.
- Stale series: P/E rebuilt from filed EPS (`pe_now_override`); EV multiples scaled by enterprise value today ÷ on the last date and flagged.
- Forward P/E (optional current FocusAlpha consensus estimates, with EPS basis and fiscal period identified) is shown in the company section, never used. "P/E distorted" when trailing ÷ forward > 1.5.
- Why not EV/Sales or FCF yield: EV/Sales rises when margins rise (it read Parker-Hannifin's margin gains as "expensive"), and FCF yield jumps with working-capital and capex timing.
- The multiples compare the stock only with its own past. They are not a valuation.

**Result: one action label per company (`result()` in screener.py).** Each label answers "should research time go here now?"; the reason is the first line under it.
- **Research now** (yes): Business green, Management not red, no accounting red flag, not short history, and either the median multiple percentile at or below the 50th (`research_now_pe`) or the direction "Getting cheaper" at any level (`cheaper_counts`, the user's option B). For the second route the lines are "Good business, getting cheaper: multiples X% below their 1-year level and Y% below a year ago" and "Still above their usual level (73rd)". Otherwise: "Good business, multiples below their usual level (41st)"; "Research line $210.32; price 2% below it" (+ " — close" when less than 5% below, `near_line_price`).
- **Quick look** (a short, time-boxed check now): an average business — Business yellow, or green with a red Management light (not short history, no red flag) — and the median percentile at or below the 33rd (`low_in_range_pe`). Lines: "Average business, but multiples low in their own history (29th)"; "Check why it is average on <measures>".
- **Research at lower price** (not yet; research has not started): the same good business as Research now, median percentile above the 50th (or not meaningful) and not getting cheaper. Lines: "Good business, multiples above their usual level (73rd)"; "Research below $434.00 (−14% from today)" (+ " — close" within 5 percentile points, `near_line_pts`). The user rejected "Watchlist" (does it mean watch or research?) and "Wait for price" (it read as research done, waiting to buy).
- **Not now** (no), with the reason first (tested in this order since v4.4: accounting red flag, too early, weak business, average business; user, 23 Oct 2026, so a company whose scores are for information only reads Too early, not Weak): "Average business, multiples not low in their own history (84th)" plus the average and weak measures; "Too early: only 2 clean years on the current business" plus "Revisit after FY<L + 3 − n> results"; "Weak business: weak on <measures>"; "Accounting red flag: <flag>; revisit when resolved". The user rejected "Average business" and "Too early to judge" as labels because they did not say whether to spend time now.
- Further lines where they apply: "Returns X% vs peers Y%: above / below / in line" (B4 median against the peer median over the same years, ±1 point; not on Not now); "Multiples disagree"; re-look signals — a new CEO within 24 months (`new_ceo_months`, from the collector's `ceo_since`) or a deal above 25% of revenue after the latest year-end — shown as "Re-look signal" on Not now and Quick look and as "Note" on the others. Industry is context, not a gate.

**The map: where each company lands (above the results table; the user asked on 2026-10-21 for a quadrant so a long list reads at a glance).** `quad_map()` in make_html.py. Rows are the Business light: Good (green), Average (yellow), Weak (red). Left to right is the median multiple percentile in the stock's own history; the divider between the two halves is the 50th (the stock's usual level), with thin lines at the 33rd and 67th. Each box is titled with its action: Good and cheaper than usual = RESEARCH NOW, Good and dearer = RESEARCH AT LOWER PRICE, Average and cheaper = QUICK LOOK (below the 33rd), Average and dearer = NOT NOW (average, not cheap), the whole Weak row = NOT NOW (weak business). Each company is a dot at its real position with its ticker: a filled blue dot is Research now, a blue ring is Research at lower price or Quick look, a small grey dot is Not now, so a dot whose label differs from its box (getting cheaper, a red Management light) shows. A green ↓ after the ticker = getting cheaper, a red ↑ = getting dearer. A narrow right column holds companies with no meaningful multiple. **Not judged yet (v4.2; the user found the one-line "Not placed" list under the map hard to read and chose this from two prototypes on 2026-10-21):** a fourth band below the Weak row, set apart by a small gap, hatched grey, labelled "Not judged yet" and titled "NOT JUDGED YET — red flag, too early after a deal, or Business light open · the dot shows only where the multiples sit". It holds every company without a Business row: accounting red flags, too-early names (fewer than 3 clean years after a deal) and a Business light still open (a missing measure decides the colour). Each sits at its real multiple percentile on the same axis (or in the no-multiple column), with a second line under the ticker giving the reason: red "red flag: <the flag>" (material weakness, SEC enforcement (AAER), …) or grey "too early · revisit FY<year>" (only "too early" in the narrow no-multiple column), or "Business light open". The band is drawn only when at least one name belongs in it, and the key under the map mentions it only then. Hover shows the label, the percentile and the first reason; a click opens the company's section. Labels just left of the 50th, and labels that would run past the right edge, sit to the left of their dot. The user chose this 2 × 2 with the action written in each box, and asked for the 67th-percentile line and the no-meaningful-multiple column; keep all three. Do not go back to a chart that must be decoded, or to text that repeats the results table: the user rejected the v3 quadrant (Business score 1–5 against P/E percentile, no labels), a dot strip with five marker styles (too many codes), a 3 × 5 ticker grid (not intuitive enough) and reason cards under the map (they repeated the results table). **Notes in a box around the ticker (v4.6 and v4.6.1; the user asked on 2026-10-23 to see what an issue is at first glance, then to put the text in a collapsible box so that other tickers never move when many companies are screened at once):** a ticker with any issue gets a box around it, closed by default, showing the ticker, a ▸ and the number of notes. The box colour is the most serious note. Red = accounting red flag ("red flag: material weakness in controls", "red flag: SEC accounting case (AAER)", "red flag: restated accounts (8-K 4.02)", "red flag: auditor qualified the accounts"). Amber = a past issue outside the red-flag horizon ("past SEC case (2016–18), not a red flag"; this replaces the v4.3.2 amber highlight) or the financial risk gate ("high debt: net debt 5.6× EBITDA", or "interest cover 1.8×"). Grey = business changing ("big deal after year-end (31% of revenue)"), a CEO in office under 24 months ("new CEO · Jul 2026"; CEOs of 2–5 years stay as the grey tag in the results table only) and multiples that disagree ("multiples disagree: P/E 78th, EV/EBITDA 39th"). The user chose amber over red for the past issue so red keeps meaning a red flag. A click on ▸ opens the notes as a panel over the map (drawn last, so it covers what is under it and moves nothing); a second click closes it; "Show all notes" above the map opens every box; a click on the ticker still opens the company section. Tickers keep their v4.5 positions: label width counts only the ticker, its arrow and the ▸, never the note text. A note near the right edge opens to the left, and the map grows at the bottom when the lowest note needs room. Names in the Not judged yet band keep their one reason line under the ticker (red flag in red, too early with the revisit year, or Business light open), because the band always had room for it; their other notes go in the box and open below that line. With many open notes on a crowded map the panels cover neighbouring tickers, which is why notes start closed. Never let a note move another ticker.

**The score build-up section (display only; `redesign.py`).** The user found the earlier section too dense to read, so each rule is shown once, the panels do not repeat the factor arithmetic, and detail sits behind links; keep it that way.
- Each part of a company section sits in its own panel with a coloured left edge, a light tint and a heading in the same colour: overview grey, accounting red flags slate, Business blue, Industry teal, Management purple, financial risk gate brown, information and perimeter light grey. No panel is green, yellow or red, because those colours belong to the lights.
- The overview opens with a Result card (the label and up to six of its lines, with "Research line $X; price Y% below it" kept on one line; the long "Detail" text is dropped because the panels repeat it) and a scorecard: tiles grouped by factor under the factor heading, which keeps its light and average ("✓ 3.8", the user asked to keep it). Each tile shows the measure's 1–5 score in a chip coloured by its light, the code, the key number (the last % or × figure before the first → of the arithmetic; M3 shows both columns; R1 shows net debt ÷ EBITDA) and a short name, and links to its row. The two gates have no score, so their chips read Pass or Fail: R1 from the gate, RF from the red-flag check. A not-scored measure shows "–" and n/a. The multiples table and P/E chart stay on the right.
- Each measure row leads with its result line in larger type, then notes, then a bar chart for any year-by-year series of 4 or more years (B1, B3, B4, I3; dashed line = median; values of 10 or more rounded to whole numbers), then the short inputs. Inputs longer than 34 characters, the rule and the sources sit behind "Full inputs", "Rule" and "Sources" links. Each rule is also listed once, in "How each measure is set" at the top of the section. Long input labels are cut at the first bracket, with the full label in a dotted-underline hover. Bold is kept for the result line and the tile numbers only.
- Red-flag rows: ✓ when clean; red ✗ with its "How checked" note open only for the check behind the company's red flag (matched from the flag label: 8-K Item 4.02, material weakness → internal control, SEC AAER, restatement to correct an error, modified audit opinion, accounting regulator finding); amber "!" with "How checked" open for a past issue outside the horizon (an AAER whose misconduct ended more than 5 years ago; the red-flag tile then reads Pass with "Past AAER" in amber); grey "–" for anything else that is not clean, such as no ICFR report yet for a newly public company or an item marked not scored.
- The Industry peer group is stated once, under the panel heading. Information and Perimeter are folded to one line each (auditor changes, CFO departures, share classes; the window sentence, number of automatic flags, deals listed, data repairs); Perimeter opens with a "window cut by a deal" tag when the window is the current perimeter.
- Every panel is collapsible (v4.5; the user asked on 2026-10-23 for Result, Accounting red flags, Business, Industry, Management and Financial risk gate to collapse like Shown for information and Perimeter and data). A click on the panel heading closes or opens it. These six open by default; a closed panel keeps its header line: the Result label and its first line, the red-flag result, each factor's light and average, and for the financial risk gate the gate result with net debt ÷ EBITDA and interest cover. A scorecard tile or any in-page link opens the closed panels around its target before scrolling there.
- No number, score, light or label changes in this section.

**Screening records (v4.3; designed with the user on 2026-10-22; vault rule 20; `vault_records.py`).** The user wanted to record why a company was not moved forward and, on later refreshes, to see whether an excluded company may have changed. The record stores the condition that excluded the company and tests on each run whether it still holds, because a screened-out company has no thesis yet; what can change is the reason it was excluded.
- One permanent note per screened company (all labels, not only Not now) in `research/screens/records/`. Frontmatter = latest state (Bases reads only frontmatter); body = a "Latest" block between `<!-- screener:latest:start/end -->` markers, a "Your notes" section, and a "History" table with one row per run, newest first, old rows never rewritten.
- **Two separate reasons.** The screener's reason (`screener_label`, `screen_reason`, `reason_line`) is written by the engine. The user's reason lives in four fields only the user fills: `our_decision` (`move forward` / `not now`; blank = not reviewed), `our_reason`, `our_reopen_if` (something observable) and `our_check_date`. Never fill, infer or reword them.
- **`screen_reason`** (closed list): `good-cheap` (Research now), `average-cheap` (Quick look), `good-not-cheap` (Research at lower price), `average-not-cheap`, `weak-business`, `too-early`, `red-flag` (the four Not now reasons), `out-of-scope`. **Reopen tests** on the next run: good-not-cheap → label becomes Research now, multiples getting cheaper, or price at or below the recorded research line; average-not-cheap → the company now counts as a good business (Business green and Management not red; the record's reopen line names the light that made it average: "Management light no longer red while the Business light stays green" for McKesson, "Business light turns green with the Management light not red" otherwise) or median percentile ≤ 33rd (v4.7; before, a green-Business, red-Management name was marked Look again with nothing changed); weak-business → Business no longer red or a red Business measure scores higher; too-early → no longer too early; red-flag → the flag is gone; every reason → a better label, a new re-look signal (new CEO, deal above 25% of revenue; compared by meaning since v4.7.1), or the user's `our_check_date` passed. `reopen_status` (renamed by the user on 2026-10-22 from closed / due / triggered, so each value says what to do): **No action** (nothing has happened), **Check now** (a date has passed: the next annual report should be out, or the user's check date; nothing tested yet), **Look again** (the reason the company was left out no longer holds, or the price reached the research line; never a buy signal). Only a full run sets a status back to No action.
- **No change, no reopen (v4.7).** A reopen condition cannot be met when nothing moved since the record (label, lights, measure scores, median percentile, price, flags, rules version): the status stays No action and the reason says to check the record. The user's own `our_check_date` still sets Look again.
- **Next check** = the date the next annual report should be out: the latest fiscal year-end moved to the next fiscal year, plus 75 days (the revisit year for too-early names). The fiscal year-end comes from the fact file (`fiscal_year_end_latest`, or the ICFR year-end); without it, one year after the run.
- **Leading indicator** (display only): `b1_latest`/`b1_median` and `b4_latest`/`b4_median`, the latest year against the window median, in the record and in the B1/B4 notes on the page. The lights use 10-year windows and 3-year medians, so a real turn in a business can take 2–3 years to change a light; these two columns show it first. They change no score, light or label.
- **Price at the screen**: `price_at_screen` and `price_date` (the date of the last daily P/E), so the returns of excluded names can later be checked against the names kept.
- **Historical upstream weekly price check** (describes the original environment; do not create or modify a schedule unless requested): for `good-not-cheap` records it compares the FocusAlpha delayed quote with the recorded `research_line` and sets **Look again**; any No action record whose `next_check` or `our_check_date` has passed is set **Check now**. It writes only `reopen_status`, `reopen_why`, `last_price_check` and `last_price`, and notifies the user. The research line is fixed at the run date (earnings and net debt of that day), so a Look again from price is a reminder; the next full run decides.
- **Screen Register views** (`Screen Register.base` in the vault): 3–7 short columns with set widths and one combined B · I · M lights column, so no view needs side-to-side scrolling (the user's request). An open Base tab in Obsidian can save its older view settings over a change made on disk: ask the user to close the tab before the Base file is rewritten.
- **Backfill** of a run made before v4.3: `vault_records.py snapshot-html <page.html> <out.json> --as-of <run date> [--fy-end <json of {ticker: {date, source}}>]`, then `write --snapshot <out.json>`. The page rounds bar labels to whole percent at 10% or more, so backfilled latest-year values are whole numbers; the record says so in 来源说明.
- The records never touch a decision page's conclusion fields, and a record's label is a research-priority call, not a buy or sell view.

**The results table.**
- Columns: rank, company, Result (label and its lines), Business light, Industry light, Management light with the CEO-change tag under it (colour and symbol only, no numbers; the number is in the hover text and in the company section), multiples in their own history (mini bar of the median percentile, the three percentiles on one line, the direction word, the 1/3/5/10-year comparison), flags (each flag label once). Nothing else: measure lights, peer groups and arithmetic sit in the company sections.
- Order: Research now, Quick look, Research at lower price, Not now; inside Not now: average, too early, weak, red flag; then by median percentile.
- The table stays the full record; the map above it is the quick read.

## Open decisions (apply the current rule and flag the effect)

Numbers are kept so that references stay valid; decision 5 is closed, and decision 10 (the definitions doc) is under Source of truth. The full text of each decision, with the cases behind it, is in `CHANGELOG.md`.

- **D1. Leverage year.** The risk gate uses the latest fiscal year, not the last twelve months, so a company that borrowed after its year-end is caught only at the next annual report.
- **D2. Pay vote.** M2 uses the latest vote only. Option: the lower of the last two votes (Melrose: 34.4% in 2025, 97.0% in 2026).
- **D3. CEO sales from option exercises.** Exercise-and-sell and sell-to-cover trades are not counted in the 30% test. Counted as sales, Woodward's M1 would fall from 3 to 2. Confirm.
- **D4. Amortization add-back with intangibles kept in capital.** B1 mixes two bases; removing the add-back changed no B1 score in 35 test names. Revisit if it starts to matter.
- **D6. Non-US disclosure gaps.** Where per-person holdings or CEO salary are not published (MTU), M1 stays unscored; non-SEC red-flag checks rest on annual reports and regulator searches.
- **D7. Controlled and founder companies.** Option: score M1 on both the controlling holder and the CEO and take the lower. Not tested.
- **D8. Lease-heavy businesses** (restaurants): lease liabilities push ROIC down. Not tested.
- **D9. Trailing GAAP P/E after write-downs and for young companies.** The median of three multiples limits the damage; a P/E history on adjusted EPS is still open.
- **D11. Universe tags are a draft** (proposed by Claude from GICS, descriptions and segment mix); the user corrects them via the CSV.
- **D12. Test thresholds set by Claude:** Quick look at the 33rd percentile, "close" within 5 points or 5% of price, disagreement at 30 points, the 12-month delay after a deal, "getting cheaper" at 10% below the 1-year median. Revisit after a few runs.
- **D13. Trend start dates are single days**, so a start on a one-off day distorts the line (MTU's 3-year start, one week after the GTF charge); the hover shows the split.
- **D14. B3 substitute with a disposal that was never restated.** The written rule names only the profit definition and recurring costs, so such a series is accepted (Crane: B3 = 4, Research now; marking the unrestated years not comparable gives Not now: too early). Confirm.
- **D15. Screening-record timing.** Next check at fiscal year-end + 75 days; the weekly price check uses the research line from the run date, which drifts between runs.
- **D16. Bases date filters untested** in the user's Obsidian: the "Check now" and "Not rescreened in 12 months" views in `Screen Register.base` use `date(x.toString())` and `today() - "365d"`.
- **D17. 8-K Item 4.02 horizon** counts 3 years from the filing date (user: keep for now), while the AAER counts from the misconduct. Option: count from the last restated period. Decide on the first real case.
- **D18. One post-deal year decides.** With one full year after a deal, that year alone sets the post-deal B1/B4 score and usually carries integration costs (WM FY2025). Accepted as cautious.
- **D19. Settlement accruals include amounts not yet settled** (non-participating subdivisions, pending matters); the whole accrual counts as debt. Option: count only amounts with a signed payment schedule.
- **D20. A derived non-current part.** When a company files only the current part and a rounded total (Cardinal Health), non-current = total − current, marked derived; for Cardinal this is precise to about ±$5m (FY2021–FY2023) or ±$50m (FY2024–FY2026).
- **D21. Losses on businesses sold are not added back to NOPAT.** M3 counts them, but B1–B4 treat them as operating costs in the year booked. Option: add them back like impairments.
- **D22. McKesson's currency-translation release.** The $47m German release has no year split and is taken against FY2021; with it M3 is 14.9% → 3, without it 15.3% → 2 (the Management light stays yellow either way). Decide how to treat a release with no year split.
- **D23. A run company's own row keeps its run window** inside its Industry group, while other group companies are cut only for separations and share jumps (CPKC: 2 years, no I1 value). Option: the group window rule for every company.
- **D24. James Hardie's asbestos liability is not counted as debt.** Payments depend on free cash flow, actuarial estimates and a cap, so it is not a fixed schedule ($128.3m current, $880.3m non-current at Mar 2026), though it is debt-like in substance. Louisiana-Pacific's $27m contingency reserves are mostly environmental and not counted. Decide whether such liabilities count.
- **D25. Deals split across two fiscal years** can pass no single year's 25% revenue test (Conagra's Pinnacle Foods, Campbell's Snyder's-Lance); set the window by hand with `perimeter_start`. Option: a second test on deal revenue ÷ prior-year revenue.
- **D26. The first full year after a big deal trips the revenue test** when it starts the window; clear it by hand with `deal_flags_ok`. Option: ignore that flag automatically.
- **D27. Japanese pay and trade data.** Ask for amounts in yen (collectors gave ¥ millions); Japan has no open-market trade reports, so the net-buyer test is not known; with only a group total of directors' pay, use the average per director and say so.
- **D28. Tax receivable agreements** (Dutch Bros, Zevia) are not counted as debt-like. Decide whether they count.

## Lessons from the test runs

Historical provider observations and old fallback recipes are preserved in `CHANGELOG.md` under “Archived provider lessons”. They do not enable Fiscal.ai or override current FocusAlpha coverage checks. For fresh runs verify cash-flow continuing/discontinued labels, unit and share basis, settlement balances versus charges, current/non-current parts, and acquisitions versus separations against original documents.

## Iterating this skill (Codex)

When the user approves a rule change: change `RULES` or the code in `SKILL_DIR/scripts/`, `RULES_VERSION` and `ENGINE_VERSION` at the top of `screener.py`, `rules_version` in `references/config_example.json`, the Rules section here and the fact brief in `references/` if a fact changed; write the rule as it now stands, without the old rule or the story of the change. Update `engine-checksums.json`; in an isolated copy re-run the last run from its `raw/`, `facts/` and `config.json` and list every company whose light or label moved. History (the user's approval, what changed, test runs, companies that moved) goes to `references/CHANGELOG.md`, with one line in the Versions list below. A new open decision goes in the list in two or three lines; delete it once decided. Keep upstream rule provenance and local source adaptations distinct; do not alter a separate Claude installation without a request.

## config.json and page_text.json

`config.json` (see `config_example.json` in the engine bundle):
- top level: `title`, `as_of`, `rules_version`, `output` (HTML file name), `universe_dir` (Step 2b), `report_language="zh-CN"` and `valuation_pipeline_required=true` for new runs. The retained `pe_default_from` is legacy display text; v4.7.2 numerically defaults to the 10-year window and only per-company `pe_from` applies the transaction delay. Do not set the legacy field expecting to alter percentile eligibility. `rules_version` may be left out; when present it must equal `RULES_VERSION` in `screener.py`, or `build` stops (v4.7.2). `build` writes `run_meta.json` (engine, rules version, build time); the page subtitle and the vault records take the rules version and the engine from it, never from text typed into the config or `page_text.json`.
- per company (keyed by ticker): `key`, `name`, `group`; optional `perimeter_start`, `perimeter_note`, `deal_flags_ok`, `post_deal_from`, `held_for_sale`, `b3_mix`, `growth_start`, `growth_start_why`, `dil_base`, `downturn`, `pe_from`, `pe_from_why`, `pe_now_override`, `measure_gaps`, `data_fixes`, `data_overrides` (`{column: {FY: value}}`), `red_flag_overrides`, `extra_flags`, `measure_notes` (keyed by B1–B4, M1–M3, R1).

`universe.json`: `name`, `status`, `min_peers`, `tags` (`{code: {parent, label, def}}`), `parents` (`{code: label}`), `companies` (`{key: {t, name, tag, why, gics, window_from?, window_why?}}`), `excluded` (`{key: reason}`).

`page_text.json` (all optional): `tab_title`, `title`, `sub`, `lead`, `moves_title`, `moves_intro`, `moves` (list of `{t, v1, why}`), `problems_title`, `problems_intro`, `problems` (list of `{title, what, fix}`), `notes` (ticker → list of sentences), `method_notes`, `pe_note`, `sources`. Leave `sub` out to get the standard subtitle ("N companies · rules version … (engine …) · prices and P/E to …"). `make_html.py` stops when `sub` or `sources` names a rules version or engine different from `run_meta.json` ("rules version X", "engine vX", "engine vX, rules Y"); a reference to an earlier run's rules in other words, such as "rerun of the 22 Oct records (rules 2026-10-21h)", is allowed.

## Files in this skill

- `scripts/screener.py`, `make_html.py`, `redesign.py`, `vault_records.py`, `shot.js`: batch scoring, HTML, records and screenshots.
- `scripts/valuation_pipeline.py`, `checked_build.py`: evidence-linked valuations, scoped repair, null eligibility guards and delivery checks; `references/valuation-reliability.md` defines their inputs and commands. `scripts/test_valuation_pipeline.py` provides offline regression cases.
- `references/fact_brief_template.md`, `config_example.json`, `engine-checksums.json`: fact schema, run configuration and local integrity checks.
- `references/universe_*.json`, `debt_like_services_distribution_transport.json`: imported tagged universes and settlement evidence; validate dates before reuse.
- `references/CHANGELOG.md`: upstream history plus the local import record. `focusalpha-normalization.md` and `gangtise-screening.md`: current data collection.
- Fiscal.ai `resolve_keys.js`, `pull_main.js`, `pull_pe.js`, `pull_ev.js`, `fiscal_exec.py` and their helper scripts are retained only for provenance and old-run compatibility, with no active route or dependency.
